name: Summerhouse remote resilience & energy
thesis: 236k+ summerhouses plus affluent/remote owners create persistent frost, outage, water and energy-control jobs, but Denmark already has unusually sophisticated niche specialists; only interoperability/exact-system gaps deserve testing.
falsifiers: combined-system integration does not create purchase intent

name: Heat-pump lifecycle / exact compatibility
thesis: Heat-pump heated dwellings and 2025 sales are growing rapidly, creating future lifecycle demand; generic systems/accessories are already mature, so opportunity must be exact model/adapter/obsolete-part friction.
falsifiers: cross-brand spare specialists fully cover Danish lifecycle needs

name: Emerging EV model aftermarket
thesis: BEV stock grew 49.6% YoY and used-EV transactions are rising. Generic Tesla is saturated; the testable edge is newly scaling non-Tesla model cohorts whose Danish accessory depth lags Germany/Sweden.
falsifiers: new-model accessory supply appears simultaneously with registrations

name: Distributed energy retrofit / monitoring
thesis: 162k+ grid-connected solar installations and high electric-asset penetration create monitoring, storage and retrofit compatibility jobs, but generic solar hardware should be assumed mature until merchant lag is proven.

name: Wood/pellet installed base
thesis: Large wood/pellet installed base creates replacement needs, but Denmark already has deep model-specific spare-parts commerce; retain as a negative/reference ecosystem rather than generic launch thesis.
falsifiers: a narrow model family has no viable Danish spares
new regulation creates a specific measurement/replacement gap

name: Dynamic-price energy control
thesis: EV/heat-pump/solar households plus open price/system data create a control/interoperability layer, but 4Power already proves strong local execution; opportunity may be integration-specific rather than generic hardware.
falsifiers: hardware retrofit requires electrician in all cases
no willingness to pay beyond energy apps
